AssumptionKind.description: The shape of a discovered environment assumption.

oneOf.description: An input held at a constant value (`en = 1`).

A CONJUNCTION of environment-input holds (`ack == 1 && escalate == 0`) — the minimal set of environment inputs that must be constrained for a two-player game to become realizable, when no single hold suffices (the design has multiple independent adversarial blockers).
A finite input schedule (a command sequence).
A synthesized positional environment strategy (1-player: the environment owns all inputs).

A LIVENESS / fairness environment assumption `GF(in == v)` — the environment input holds `v` INFINITELY OFTEN — under which an unrealizable RECURRENCE (Büchi) game `GF good` becomes realizable (`GF a → GF good`, the GR(1) 1-pair objective). Distinct from `InputHold` (a SAFETY hold `G(a)`): fairness is strictly weaker (the environment may violate `a` finitely often).

A CONJUNCTION of fairness assumptions `GF(e_1 == v_1) ∧ … ∧ GF(e_k == v_k)` — the minimal set of environment liveness assumptions under which an unrealizable RECURRENCE game becomes realizable (`(⋀_i GF a_i) → GF good`, the MULTI-pair GR(1) objective), when no SINGLE fairness assumption suffices (multiple independent liveness blockers). The fairness analog of `InputConjunction`.

CellSource.description: Where a trace cell lives in the RTL (2026-10-29).

assigned.description: The `always` block(s) of the flop(s) driving a register; empty for an input.

cell.description: The cell as the trace names it (the net; a hierarchical name keeps its dots).

CexCellView.description: One register's concrete value in a counterexample state. mununu#723 — a cell wider than 64 bits was silently absent from the trace (OpenTitan edn's 109-bit `tl_i`, the bus write behind the fatal alert). `value` is unchanged for every cell that fits 64 bits — exactly the cells that were listed before — and `null` for a wider value; `hex` and `bits` are always present.

hex.description: `0x` + the value zero-padded to the cell's width — the form that always holds it.

value.description: The value when it fits 64 bits, else `null` (read `hex`).

DiscoveredAssumption.description: See [`VerdictRefinement::holds_under`]. A CONDITIONAL result: the property holds under `phi`. (Populated in Phase 2.)

engine.description: The engine that discovered it, for provenance.

non_vacuous.description: True iff `good` is genuinely reached under `phi` (the non-vacuity gate passed).

phi.description: A human-readable predicate over named inputs (Phase 2b may carry a typed schedule/strategy).

GameObjective.description: The two-player game winning objective (`objective` field). Mirrors the CLI `--objective`.

oneOf.description: Force `good` at least ONCE — the reachability game `μX. good ∨ ⟨ctrl⟩X`.
Force `good` INFINITELY OFTEN — the Büchi game `νZ.μY. (good ∧ ⟨ctrl⟩Z) ∨ ⟨ctrl⟩Y`.

MealyEntry.description: One control-state row of a [`MealyStrategy`]: the controller's response(s) at that control value.

complete.description: `false` = the reactive-move enumeration hit its bound and `moves` is a partial cover (only for wide-environment reactive states; never for the Moore fast-path). No silent truncation.

moves.description: The controller's move(s). A single `env_inputs`-empty move = a Moore (env-independent) response; several moves = a genuinely reactive response, one per environment input valuation.

rank.description: The attractor rank (distance to `good`); 0 = already `good` (no move needed).

state_value.description: The value of the strategy's state register.

MealyMove.description: One `(environment-input guard → forced controllable inputs)` move of a Mealy controller ([`MealyStrategy`]). The game is Mealy — the environment moves and the controller RESPONDS ([`ExactModel::cpre_controllable`], `∀env ∃ctrl`) — so the controller's move may depend on the current environment input. `env_inputs` is empty for an env-independent (Moore) move.

env_inputs.description: The environment-input valuation this move responds to; empty = env-independent (holds for every environment move).

forced_ctrl.description: The controllable inputs the controller forces in response.

RepairCandidate.description: One repair candidate (2026-10-30): a register whose next-state function, freed at `cycles`, lets the property survive the trace with the trace's inputs fixed.

cycles.description: The steps at which the override acts (the transition out of each).

lines.description: The statements that write the register (the candidate lines to read).

reads_property.description: The property reads this register directly: a change here changes what is measured, not what happens — reported, in its own bucket.

values.description: The value the override gives the register at each of `cycles`, as hex.

RepairStatus.description: What limited a localisation: `done` | `partial` | `none` | `unavailable`, with the reason.

ReplayResultView.description: The replay's verdict: the bench ran under Verilator and compared the trace cycle by cycle, or could not run and says why (2026-10-29).

assertions.description: Verilator's `Assertion failed` lines: the design's own assertion firing on the final state.

checks.description: The (cycle, register) comparisons the bench makes.

log.description: The bench's own lines: verdict, mismatches, assertions, the VCD line.

reason.description: Why the replay could not run (`unavailable`): Verilator or `make` missing, a compile error.

vcd_bytes.description: `replay.vcd`'s size in bytes, when `make trace` wrote it.

SourceLoc.description: A place in the RTL: the file's basename and a line (yosys's `src` keeps the path and the column; the report keeps what a reader opens).

forced_inputs.description: The inputs the strategy FORCES in this state (name → value). An input that some rank-decreasing move leaves free is omitted, so a nonempty map is the minimal driving discipline. The SAME input appearing with DIFFERENT forced values across rows is the positional obligation, made explicit as a map rather than read off a single trace.

rank.description: Attractor distance to `good` (`0` = the state already satisfies `good`).

state_value.description: The value of the strategy's state register in this row.

makefile.description: `Makefile`; it names the sources as the request named them.

skipped.description: Cells left out of the comparison, with the reason.

Trace.description: The one counterexample shape of 0.5, shared by every verb that returns a path: RTL rows fill `state` / `inputs` / `faults`, CTXDSL rows fill `state_name` / `labels`. A two-player strategy stays its own object, and the counterstrategy graph stays a view.

localization.description: `done` (every candidate register was queried), `partial` (a cap or budget cut the query short — `reason` says what), `none` (no single-register change avoids the violation within the trace's length) or `unavailable` (no trace to fix inputs from, the model could not be queried). Absent when `--localize` was not requested.

loop_start.description: For a `lasso`: the index into `steps` the last step loops back to.

repair_candidates.description: Repair candidates (2026-10-30, `--localize`): with this trace's inputs fixed, the registers whose next-state function, if free at the named cycles, would let the property survive the whole trace — candidates, never causes ([`crate::adapter::btor2::repair`]). Empty when localisation was not requested or found none; `localization` says which.

sources.description: Where each cell the trace shows lives in the RTL (2026-10-29): the legend, in the order of the first step's cells. Empty when the source map is unavailable (`diagnostics.source_map`).

unreachable_target.description: For `unreachable`: the target atoms no path reaches.

hex.description: The value in hexadecimal, at any width.

value.description: The value written, when it fits 64 bits.

oneOf.description: Reset → the failing step (a safety violation).
Reset → a prefix → a cycle repeated forever (`loop_start` marks it): a liveness stall.
Reset → a closed trap the target is never reached from again (a refuted `AG EF`).
No path: the `unreachable_target` atoms are never reached from reset (a refuted `EF`).
Reset → the injections of a fault attack that reaches its target (`steps[].faults`).

dir.description: Where the CLI wrote the files (`--emit-testbench DIR/<property>`); absent over HTTP.

gtkw.description: `replay.gtkw` — a GTKWave save file listing the clock, the trace's inputs and the registers it names, so `gtkwave replay.vcd replay.gtkw` opens on the scene (2026-10-29).

result.description: The bench built and run (`--replay` / `replay: true`); absent when not requested.

TraceStep.description: One step of a [`Trace`]: the state at `cycle` and what drives the step out of it.

inputs.description: The input assignment of this cycle (RTL), so the trace can be replayed.

labels.description: The labels of the transition out of this step (CTXDSL).

monitor.description: Cells the verifier added to the model (see [`is_monitor_cell`]): the property monitor's latches, `$past` shadows, fault-rewrite state. Kept for debugging, apart from `state`.

state.description: Register cells (RTL); empty for a CTXDSL step, which names its state in `state_name`.

TwoPlayerStrategy.description: P2.5-F — a synthesized TWO-PLAYER strategy for the controllable-reachability game `μX. (good ∨ ⟨ctrl⟩X)`: the CONTROLLER's Mealy strategy when it is realizable, or the ENVIRONMENT's positional COUNTERSTRATEGY when it is not (by determinacy, exactly one holds). The asymmetry is intrinsic to the Mealy game (`∀env ∃ctrl`): the environment is the first-mover, so its winning strategy is positional (state-indexed); the controller responds, so its strategy may depend on the environment input.

oneOf.description: The controller wins from the initial state (spec realizable) — its Mealy strategy. Serializes as `{"kind": "controller_strategy", "state_register": …, "entries": […]}`.

entries.description: One row per reachable control-state value, sorted by rank then value.

state_register.description: The state register the strategy is indexed by.

oneOf.description: The environment wins (unrealizable) — its positional counterstrategy, forcing environment inputs (robust to every controllable move) to keep the play out of the controller's winning region. Serializes as `{"kind": "environment_counterstrategy", "state_register": …, "entries": […]}`.

entries.description: One row per reachable value of `state_register`, ordered by rank then value.

state_register.description: The state register the strategy is indexed by (the register named in the `good` atom).

attack_exists.description: With `faults`: `realizable` read as "an attack wins against every environment behaviour".

controllable.description: The controller-owned inputs, echoed for provenance.

detail.description: Whose objective `outcome` is about, in words (the `--fault` polarity is stated here).

fault.description: With `faults`: the posture, as one label.

holds_under.description: Discovered environment assumption(s) under which the (unrealizable) game becomes realizable — each a CONDITIONAL `HoldsUnder(φ)` (never flips `realizable`). Only when `discover_assumptions` was requested and the game is unrealizable; empty otherwise.

objective.description: The winning objective decided, echoed for provenance (`reach` or `recurrence`).

outcome.description: The verdict envelope: `holds` | `violated` for the property [`game_outcome`] describes.

realizable.description: `true` = the controller can force `good` against every environment move (the spec is realizable); `false` = the environment can prevent it (unrealizable). For `objective = "recurrence"` this is "force `good` infinitely often" (the Büchi game).

strategy.description: The winner's strategy: a `controller_strategy` (Mealy) or an `environment_counterstrategy` (positional) — the [`crate::adapter::btor2::symbolic_bitblast::TwoPlayerStrategy`] serialized with a `"kind"` tag. For `objective = "reach"` it is the controller's attractor strategy when realizable, else the environment's positional counterstrategy. For `objective = "recurrence"` it is the CONTROLLER's Büchi strategy (force `good` infinitely often) when realizable, and `null` when not — the unrealizable recurrence witness is `stall_lasso` below. **Present only for a STATE-register `good`**: the strategy is state-indexed, so it is omitted (`null`) for a combinational-output / relational target (a FIFO's `full_o`), where `realizable` + `holds_under` still apply.

strategy_error.description: Why `strategy` is absent when the verdict is known: the extraction's own error (e.g. a goal over no state register). Absent when a strategy was extracted or none was asked for.

trace.description: P2.5-F (b) — the ENVIRONMENT STARVATION LASSO (a `lasso` [`Trace`]) for an unrealizable RECURRENCE game: a concrete play (reset → repeating `¬good` `cycle`, with the env's per-step `inputs`) proving the environment can starve `good` forever — the actionable Büchi counterpart of `realizable = false`. Present only for `objective = "recurrence"` when unrealizable AND a simple reachable force-`¬good`-forever region exists; `null` for realizable games, the `reach` objective (whose witness is `strategy`), or a subtler co-Büchi with no such region.
